text:
ravi (sales): FYI — DeckHand POC goes live tomorrow. They need a drop-in replacement for CompetitorZ's /api/respond and /api/extract endpoints. Main asks: identical UX for search+extract, pricing parity vs their bundle, and completed procurement security sheet. @sasha can you own preflight?

sasha (solutions): On it. Quick presales checklist: 1) endpoint contract mapping 2) tokenizer delta sample (200 prompts) 3) prompt envelope + metadata preservation 4) retry & timeout mapping 5) parity harness + scoring 6) pricing scenarios to mirror bundles 7) procurement answers for HSM/KMS/SLA.

mo (eng): Adapter plan: tiny node proxy that accepts CompetitorZ payloads and forwards to Redwood with schema translation + token normalization. Example mapping:
```bash
# client -> adapter
POST /api/respond {"query":"<PROMPT>","max":250}
# adapter -> redwood
POST /v1/complete {"input":"<PROMPT>","max_total_tokens":250,"stop":["---END---"]}
```We observed an initial token delta of ~-4% on a 120-sample run (Redwood tokenizes fewer tokens for these prompts). Will run 200 samples to confirm.

hema (security): Procurement wants EU data residency proof, KMS options, HSM evidence, and per-customer audit exports. Short answers: EU region pinning available in Private; customer-managed KMS with CMKs via AWS KMS supported for Dedicated/Private; HSM via validated partner (legal required); audit log exports to S3 or SIEM supported. Need the highlighted PDF.

taylor (sales-eng): Pricing note — CompetitorZ sells 50k-call bundles. Options to propose: A) token-equivalent (apply measured delta) B) flat-call mapping using avg tokens/call C) committed throughput with migration credit. Since delta looks favorable (-4%), we can show a cost-competitive token mapping and optionally include a one-month credit to reduce churn risk. I'll draft three example invoices for 50k calls.

anya (cs): Canary ops suggestion: run synthetic parity tests (same prompts + seeds) first, then 5% live traffic for 24h. Failback rule: auto switch to CompetitorZ if error rate >0.8% over 5m or structured-extract F1 drops >4%. Capture diffs in a CSV for triage.

mo (eng): Response diffs typically from sampling defaults, stop-seq handling, and subtle tokenization whitespace rules. Mitigations: 1) set explicit temperature=0.0 in adapter for deterministic POC 2) add explicit stop sequence (see example) 3) post-normalize whitespace & punctuation 4) token rebalance shim to map token counts before billing.

sasha (solutions): Eval harness plan: small node script to call both endpoints, record token counts, outputs, and compute a parity score (field match ratio + normalized edit distance + token delta). It will output JSONL per prompt for product triage.

hema (security): For the procurement sheet: I'll draft answers (EU pinning, CMK support, audit export details) by tomorrow 11:00. Please upload highlights. Note: HSM proof requires procurement + partner contact; that will add a 2-week lead for contractual addendum.

ravi (sales): Uploaded the questionnaire and flagged three highest-priority items: EU residency proof, HSM capability, and POC SLA >=99.7%. They also requested sample IPs for staging.

mo (eng): I'll DM a /28 ephemeral IP block for staging and NAT details. Adapter logs will redact PII by default; can enable additional redaction rules per-customer.

taylor (sales-eng): I'll prepare the three pricing scenarios and include a suggested migration credit (15% first-month) in one option.

canary-bot: Canary scheduled: deckhand-adapter -> canary-2026-04-08T07:00Z (5% traffic). Prechecks: unit tests, 200-sample tokenizer run, parity harness.

sasha (solutions): Action items (owners): 1) 200-prompt tokenizer run -> mo (EOD) 2) adapter stub + mapping doc -> mo (tomorrow 09:00) 3) procurement answers -> hema + legal (tomorrow 11:00) 4) pricing scenarios -> taylor (tomorrow COB) 5) eval harness & parity score -> sasha + mo (initial by day 1 of POC) 6) canary runbook + failback -> anya (pre-canary).

ravi (sales): Thanks all — quick sync 08:30 tomorrow for 10m. Ping here if blocked or tag me. :shipit:
